summary: Independently verify the finite endpoint identity for the recorded degree range: required degrees 4..32 minus recorded degrees 4..25 equals exactly 26..32. The script emits all explicit finite inputs and its asserted result.
script:
import json
import hashlib
required_start, required_end = 4, 32
recorded_start, recorded_end = 4, 25
required = list(range(required_start, required_end + 1))
recorded = list(range(recorded_start, recorded_end + 1))
missing = [d for d in required if d not in set(recorded)]
expected = [26, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32]
assert missing == expected
assert len(missing) == 7
assert all(26 <= d <= 32 for d in missing)
assert all(d not in missing for d in recorded)
payload = {"requiredDegreeRange":[required_start,required_end],"recordedDegreeRange":[recorded_start,recorded_end],"requiredDegrees":required,"recordedDegrees":recorded,"setDifferenceRequiredMinusRecorded":missing,"expectedMissingDegrees":expected,"identityVerified":missing==expected,"interpretation":"The finite range comparison verifies only that the supplied record, whose degree summaries end at 25, omits degrees 26 through 32. It does not compute any ordered basis, labelled Pieri row, or Smith form."}
encoded = json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')).encode()
payload["outputSha256"] = hashlib.sha256(encoded).hexdigest()
print(json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True))
